passage: Between 2000 and 2020, the world's yearly harvest from wild fisheries and aquaculture (the farming of fish, shellfish, and aquatic plants) grew by about 75 million metric tons. An analyst claims that nearly all of this growth came from aquaculture: the wild catch held almost steady for two decades, while aquaculture production kept climbing in every five-year period.

questionTable.caption: World wild-capture fisheries and aquaculture production, 2000-2020 (approximate)

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the claim?

choices.text: Wild capture reached its highest level in 2000, at 96.2 million metric tons, and then fell to 89.7 million metric tons by 2010, the lowest level shown.
Aquaculture production grew from 43.1 million metric tons in 2000 to 122.8 million in 2020, rising in every year shown.
In 2000 aquaculture production was 43.1 million metric tons, while wild capture was 96.2 million metric tons.
From 2000 to 2020 wild capture stayed between 89.7 and 96.2 million metric tons, while aquaculture rose every five years, from 43.1 to 122.8 million.

explanation:
**Choice D is correct.** The claim has two parts: the wild catch held almost steady, and aquaculture production kept climbing. Only D reports both: wild-capture figures stayed within a narrow band (89.7 to 96.2 million metric tons) while aquaculture rose in every five-year period.

**The Full Solution:**
- Part 1 of the claim: the wild catch barely changed from 2000 to 2020.
- Part 2: aquaculture production rose in every period shown.
- D gives the wild-capture range and the aquaculture rise from 43.1 to 122.8 million metric tons, covering both parts.

**Why the other choices are wrong:**
- A: It describes a fall in the wild catch but says nothing about aquaculture growth.
- B: It supports only the aquaculture half of the claim; it leaves out the steady wild catch.
- C: It gives a single year, so it cannot show either the steady wild catch or the rising aquaculture figures.
